items.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
items.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs.

items.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
items.summary: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

items.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
items.summary: Global Workspace Theory (GWT), a leading theory of consciousness, holds that information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialized processes that use it. Building a workspace into a network does not reveal what the trained network computes with it: a module that reports an answer may have combined a broadcast message with its own knowledge, or merely forwarded an answer computed elsewhere, and task accuracy and ablation cannot tell these apart.

items.title: A Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Optimization of Benchmark Test Functions using Entangled Qutrits
items.summary: Typically, quantum genetic algorithms are based on qubits, a two-level quantum system. This work investigates the optimization of Rastrigin, Rosen-Brock and Table Holder Function in comparison with Classical Genetic Algorithm (CGA), using two quantum approaches: Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA), and Higher-Order Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HO-QGA) based on qutrits, a three-level system.

items.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
items.summary: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.
items.source: The American Journal of Applied Sciences

items.title: Multimodal Coma Stimulation to Improve Arousal and Physical Function in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury
items.summary: Background: Impaired consciousness is one of the most serious complications following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Sensory deprivation may delay neural recovery and worsen patient outcomes.

items.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
items.summary: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future e + e − colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes e + e − → t t ‾ , e + e − → μ + μ − and Bhabha scattering e + e − → e + e − , representing the mass threshold behavior, the Z pole resonance and the s / t -channel interplay.

items.title: Nondiagonal Lindblad master equations in quantum reservoir engineering
items.summary: Reservoir engineering has proven to be a practical approach to control open quantum systems, preserving quantum coherence by appropriately manipulating the reservoir and system-reservoir interactions. In this context, for systems comprised of different parts, it is common to describe the dynamics of a subsystem of interest by performing an adiabatic elimination of the remaining components of the system.

items.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
items.summary: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

items.title: Gravitational self-interaction mitigates superluminal signalling
items.summary: The Schrödinger-Newton equation aims at describing the dynamics of massive quantum systems subject to the gravitational self-interaction. As a deterministic nonlinear quantum wave equation, it is generally believed to conflict with the relativistic no-signalling principle.

items.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
items.summary: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks.

items.title: C2 |Q⟩: A Robust Framework for Bridging Classical and Quantum Software Development
items.summary: Quantum Software Engineering (QSE) is emerging as a critical discipline to make quantum computing accessible to a broader developer community; however, most quantum development environments still require developers to engage with low-level details across the software stack—including problem encoding, circuit construction, algorithm configuration, hardware selection and result interpretation—making them difficult for classical software engineers to use. To bridge this gap, we present C2 \(|{\rm{Q}}\rangle\) , a…

items.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
items.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices.

items.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy.

items.title: Entanglement, records, and quantum recovery in qubit chains
items.summary: We investigate entanglement, readable records and quantum recovery using an exactly solvable chain of sequentially interacting qubits. For weak interactions, entanglement reaches a later environment site before that site carries an equally strong local record.

items.title: Adaptive Hamiltonian Identification via Quantum Reinforcement Learning under Non-Stationary Dynamics
items.summary: Accurate identification of the Hamiltonian governing a quantum system is important for quantum-system characterization, device calibration, simulation, and reliable operation of quantum hardware. In practical systems, however, the governing dynamics may vary over time because of parameter drift, changing control conditions, or transitions between operating regimes.

items.title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
items.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical learning architectures provide a promising framework for integrating quantum feature transformations into complex data-processing tasks. Among these transformations, the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) offers a structured approach to feature processing, motivating an investigation of how its circuit configuration influences predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness.

items.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
items.summary: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties.

items.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
items.summary: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

items.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
items.summary: The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

items.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
items.summary: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron’s position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

items.title: Canine cognitive dysfunction: an updated review of mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical management
items.summary: Canine cognitive dysfunction (CCD) is a common age-associated neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive changes in memory, learning, spatial orientation, social interaction, and awareness, with adverse consequences for canine welfare and caregiver quality of life. In addition to its clinical importance in veterinary medicine, CCD shares several behavioral and neuropathological features with Alzheimer’s disease (AD), making affected dogs a valuable comparative model of human brain aging.

items.title: Therapeutic communication: avoidance of negative influences and application of beneficial suggestions in anesthesia and intensive care, emergency, and pain medicine
items.summary: In anesthesia, and in emergency and intensive care medicine a “therapeutic communication” with the patient is needed that exceeds mere information exchange and that supports patient and treatment. First, ever-present nocebo effects and negative suggestions must be avoided or neutralized.

items.title: Quantum machine learning for quantitative finance
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) and quantum ML (QML) have gained significant importance, as they offer powerful tools for tackling complex computational problems across various domains. An overview of QML’s uses in quantitative finance is presented here.

items.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
items.summary: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear.

items.title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
items.summary: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward.

items.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
items.summary: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution.

items.title: Noetics, a New but Old Understanding of Mind and Reality
items.summary: Noetics is examined here as an interdisciplinary approach to how lived experience becomes a knowledge claim and informs action. This narrative review brings historical philosophy into dialogue with cognitive science, contemporary theories of consciousness, contemplative traditions, and artificial intelligence.
items.source: Journal of Advanced Research in Social Sciences

items.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
items.summary: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

items.title: Toward a Composite Framework of Consciousness: Integrating Brain–Body Interactions, Sentience, and Neuroimaging in Disorders of Consciousness
items.summary: The accurate assessment of consciousness in non-communicative patients remains a major challenge for neuroscience and clinical care. While behavioral scales such as the Coma Recovery Scale–Revised (CRS-R) provide standardized tools for diagnosis, they are limited by patients’ motor impairments and the absence of subjective report.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schr\"odinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle-hole-invariant momenta fix the bulkinvariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: The waggle dance in honeybees: a language - beyond metaphor
items.summary: The waggle dance reports an outbound flight vector with a ritualized whole-body movement to a location in the environment surrounding the bee colony. This informative gesture is embedded in the cognitive faculties involved in organizing the social life inside and outside the hive during foraging for food and finding a new nest site.

Philosophy and Cognitive Sciences in the Study of Creative Activity of Consciousness” (Moscow, Saint Petersburg: Tsentr gumanitarnykh initsiativ, 2025).

items.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing
items.summary: Pharmacological agents and brain stimulation can modulate conscious states, but offer limited control over the structure of the experience itself. Virtual reality (VR) can alter subjective experience while allowing its structure to be experimentally controlled.

items.title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
items.summary: Studies of relativistic quantum information in noninertial and black-hole settings often focus on specific input states and resource functionals, leaving the common origin of recurring monotonic trends in quantum resources and correlations unclear. In this work, we identify a common channel-ordering structure from the complementary exterior and interior reductions of the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation, representing the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, respectively.

items.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
items.summary: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically.

items.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
items.summary: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

items.title: Quantum Sensing as an Optimization-Inference Stack
items.summary: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision limit.

items.title: Parameter-shift rules for gradients in boson sampling experiments
items.summary: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive n th order parameter-shift rules (PSRs) for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where n photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that one cannot naturally generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling.

items.title: Almost-quantum correlations violate information causality
items.summary: Information causality (IC), a generalization of the no-signalling principle, states that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

items.title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
items.summary: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain.

items.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows.

items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison.

items.title: Endogenous suspension of phenomenal consciousness during extended cessation: Regional homogeneity analysis of multi-participant 7T fMRI of an advanced meditative endpoint
items.summary: Extended cessation (EC) is a rare advanced meditative state characterized by the voluntary absence of reportable phenomenal experience, followed by reproducible aftereffects including immense mental clarity, equanimity, and peace. EC offers an endogenous model for investigating the mechanisms of consciousness.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

items.title: Physical predictions in closed quantum gravity
items.summary: Recent developments in gravitational path integrals indicate that the nonperturbative physical Hilbert space of a closed universe is one-dimensional within each superselection sector. This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities?

items.title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
items.summary: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states.

items.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
items.summary: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field.

items.title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
items.summary: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence.

items.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
items.summary: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art.

items.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear.

items.title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
items.summary: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult.

items.title: Authenticating quantum key distribution through random position checks
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) requires some form of authentication in order for the parties to be sure they are not unknowingly generating a key with an adversary pretending to be one of the honest parties. In this work, we propose a protocol in which the position of one of the parties is used as the authentication credential for key distribution.

items.title: On the design of sequential quantum repeaters with error detection
items.summary: Long-distance, trust-free quantum communications rely on the development of scalable quantum repeater schemes. Sequential entanglement generation with error detection is a promising approach that combines manageable implementation requirements with a hop-by-hop architecture compatible with existing classical infrastructure.

items.title: Hamiltonian Stabilization of the Two-Photon Dicke Model
items.summary: Collective two-photon light--matter interactions enable pair amplification but can destroy spectral confinement, preventing a stable thermodynamic bright phase. We show that a positive Kac-scaled number-Kerr interaction renders the two-photon Dicke Hamiltonian of \(N\) emitters lower-bounded at all couplings while preserving its generalized \(\mathbb Z_4\) symmetry.

items.title: When the Noise Gets Noisy: Quantum Error Correction with Disordered Noise and Misinformed Decoding
items.summary: Experimental demonstrations of quantum error correction often exhibit noise that varies across space and time, and attempting to characterize this disorder has been shown to substantially improve decoding performance. However, theoretical studies of quantum error correction typically assume fixed, perfectly known, homogeneous noise.

items.title: Optimal Error corrected Hamiltonian estimation with nuisance parameters
items.summary: Realistic quantum sensing is often affected by both noise and unknown nuisance parameters. Under Markovian dynamics, existing error correction approaches have often sought to suppress nuisance responses alongside environmental noise.

items.title: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping
items.summary: Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. We study its security in a noisy network whose intermediate nodes perform the quantum operations faithfully but may misreport the classical outcome that end users rely on.

items.title: Tunable Ground-State Entanglement in Fully Connected Quantum Systems: From Logarithmic to Volume-Law Scaling
items.summary: Entanglement scaling is a central probe of the complexity of quantum many-body ground states, yet once geometric locality is absent, it can depend sensitively on the structure and normalization of interactions. For fully connected Hamiltonians with the natural Kac normalization, nondegenerate gapped ground states are known to obey a logarithmic entanglement bound.

items.title: Non-Binary Detector Error Models
items.summary: A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty. Such circuit-level noise is commonly described by a detector error model (DEM).

items.title: Efficient Classical Algorithms for Ground Energy Estimation of Fermions with Conjugate-Pair Orbital Interactions
items.summary: Estimating the ground energy of interacting fermions is central to quantum many-body physics, and recent quantum algorithms provide polynomial-time guarantees for some structured families. Classical approaches commonly rely on quantum Monte Carlo, where the sign problem is a major obstacle.

items.title: Imaginary-Time Density Correlations Encode Quantum Entropy and Free Energy
items.summary: In the classical limit, maximum-entropy inference yields an estimate of the excess entropy from the static structure factor through a single momentum sum. Quantum mechanically this estimate fails, because interactions also change the kinetic energy, while delocalization and exchange add information that equal-time correlations do not contain.

items.title: Effect of coupling asymmetry on the spontaneous decay and entanglement of two atoms in a common cavity
items.summary: We investigate the dynamics and the spontaneous decay of two identical two-level atoms into the vacuum in a cavity at low temperature. We analytically derive the survival probability and the amplitudes of the state of the system by calculating the exact self-energy when the atoms are both initially excited.

items.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
items.summary: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit.

items.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
items.summary: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $μ^+μ^-\toγγγ$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events.

items.title: Quantifying the irrealism required by quantum random access codes
items.summary: How far must decoding observables be from having elements of reality to achieve a given quantum advantage in a communication task? We answer this question for quantum random access codes.

items.title: Stitching Quantum Codes into Quilts: Universal Logic with no Ancillary Qubits
items.summary: Proposals abound for performing fault-tolerant logical Pauli-product measurements between quantum codes beyond the surface code. We introduce a new construction, the code quilt, whereby a target joint logical operator of two or more codeblocks is directly measured without the use of an ancillary system.

items.title: All Non-Contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are Free-Fermion in Disguise
items.summary: Decomposing Hamiltonians into classically tractable fragments is central to quantum simulation. One such way of doing so is the contextual subspace decomposition, which expresses the Hamiltonian with respect to non-contextual sets of Paulis.

items.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
items.summary: Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph.

items.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
items.summary: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations.

items.title: A sensitivity-constrained polynomial method for DQC1 query complexity
items.summary: The polynomial method is one of the fundamental techniques for proving lower bounds on quantum query complexity, particularly in the BQP query model. In this work, we develop an analogue of the polynomial method for the DQC1 query model.

items.title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
items.summary: Variational quantum circuit synthesis jointly searches circuit structure and continuous parameters to reduce costly two-qubit gates, but block-based workflows typically instantiate blocks independently, limiting simplification across block boundaries. Moreover, fully unitary synthesis does not exploit opportunities created by permitted output measurements and classical feedforward.

items.title: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir
items.summary: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts.

items.title: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain
items.summary: Single-photon emitters are one of the key elements in state-of-the art quantum technologies, yet optimizing and manipulating their emission requires precise fabrication of the emitter systems themselves. Here, we propose a route to tailored single-photon emission by exploiting cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain.

items.title: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution
items.summary: In quantum communications and other photon-counting applications, reliably detecting weak optical signals against a strong noise background remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we develop a simple idea: when a signal is carried by pairs (or more generally multiplets) of photons emitted simultaneously, postselection of coincident detections recorded on two detectors makes it possible to improve-sometimes drastically-the Signal to Noise Ratio.

items.title: The role of complementarity and quantum correlation in the uncertainty relations and the optimum states
items.summary: Uncertainty relations are used in quantum mechanics to illustrate the complementarity of two observables, assuming there is a lower bound for the product of their dispersions that depends on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of those observables in an optimum state. In this work, we demonstrate that the complex parameter of the optimum state equation has real and imaginary parts that depend on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation between the observables in…

items.title: Ellis: Extremely Fast Quantum Circuit Simulation under Qubit Loss and Leakage
items.summary: Qubit loss and leakage are persistent errors: while a qubit remains lost or leaked, every operation acting on it is dropped. Consequently, the Clifford circuit executed differs from shot to shot.

items.title: A receiver-side approach to confirm phase randomization in BB84 time-bin QKD with weak coherent pulses
items.summary: In quantum cryptography using time-bin BB84 protocols, the relative phase of symbol pulses has to be random to avoid vulnerability to coherent attacks. Typically this phase randomization is checked on the sender side.

items.title: Local-channel inequivalence within analytic symmetry-broken phases
items.summary: Gibbs states at different temperatures can be inequivalent under two-way quasi-local channels even within a single phase with spontaneously broken continuous symmetry and analytic free energy. We prove this for the symmetry-invariant Gibbs states of a canonical ideal Bose gas at fixed density and a classical vortex-free Villain model on hypercubic lattices in $d\ge3$ dimensions.

items.title: The classical complexity of quantum state transmission
items.summary: Quantum communication provides a natural means to transmit quantum information, but how difficult is it to make such a transmission using only classical communication resources? We address this question by introducing classical communication models for quantum preparations and defining their minimum cost as the classical complexity.

items.title: Genuinely Out-of-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation
items.summary: Bose-Einstein (BE) condensation typically occurs in the ground state. Prominent exceptions include excitons, whose ground state is the vacuum; consequently, they undergo BE condensation only in out-of-equilibrium regimes to counteract rapid decay.

items.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
items.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult.

items.title: The influence of quantum scarring on the onset of Bohmian chaos
items.summary: In the present work we investigate how the stable and unstable periodic orbits of a perturbed two-dimensional oscillator influence the Bohmian trajectories of the corresponding quantum system. In particular, we find that in our systems all Bohmian trajectories become chaotic in the long run and examine the times needed for them to approach their ergodic pattern.

items.title: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices
items.summary: Flat bands support compact localized states (CLSs), whereas bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain spatially localized despite having energies embedded in the continuum of extended states. Here, we investigate the connection between these phenomena in a class of one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices whose Bloch Hamiltonians take the pseudospin form H(k)=d(k)S.

items.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
items.summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG).

items.title: A New Quantum Algorithm Framework for Integer Order Entropy Estimation
items.summary: Entropy estimation for unknown distributions is a basic problem in statistical property estimation. In this paper, we propose a quantum algorithm framework for estimating Rényi entropy with fixed integer order $k\geq 2$.

items.title: High-fidelity control of long-lived data qubits via a noisy mediator
items.summary: Long-lived qubits are attractive for storing quantum information, but they are often difficult to control or couple directly. A common strategy is to use mediator qubits to generate effective interactions for gate implementation.

items.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
items.summary: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution.

items.title: Nonmagnetic Impurity Effects on Majorana Braiding Quantum Gates in Vortex Cores
items.summary: Using time-dependent many-body simulations, we investigate nonmagnetic impurity effects on vortex-core Majorana braiding. In the two-MZM $\sqrt{Z}$ gate, sufficiently strong attractive impurities suppress the topological gap $Δ_t$, reduce adiabaticity, and degrade the quantization of the geometric-phase difference; the repulsive impurities considered here cause no comparable damage despite stronger zero-energy nonequilibrium local density of states (LDOS) distortions.

items.title: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle
items.summary: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle).

items.title: Moiré-Enabled Recursive Phase Unwrapping for Differential Atom Interferometry
items.summary: Weak equivalence principle tests comparing different elements may be more sensitive to violations than those comparing isotopes. However, differences in effective wave vector complicate common-mode rejection of vibration noise.

items.title: Structure-Guided Synthesis of Low-Error Syndrome Extraction Circuits
items.summary: Gate orders can change fault propagation and logical error rates even when syndrome-extraction circuits implement the same ideal stabilizer measurements. Optimizing these orderings independently for every check, however, becomes computationally demanding as code size increases.

items.title: Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Differential Privacy
items.summary: Differential privacy has been successfully extended to quantum computing and information processing, where sensitive data are encoded in quantum states and protected by quantum noise mechanisms that keep the outcomes of any measurement on neighboring states nearly indistinguishable. In the quantum setting, however, the state submitted to a quantum computer may be entangled with a hidden reference system secretly held by an adversary.

items.title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
items.summary: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size.

items.title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
items.summary: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) can recover information about ideal quantum computations from noisy circuit executions, but may require a large sampling overhead. Fundamental lower bounds show that recovering noiseless observables without problem-specific information can require superpolynomially many samples, with exponential overhead for broad classes of noisy circuits.

items.title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates that can be implemented efficiently across multiple qubit pairs. We present a scheme for simultaneous pairwise entangling operations, i.e., a transversal controlled-$Z$ gate, across neighboring wells in a double-well trapped-ion architecture.

items.title: Insurance portfolio simulation with a quantum circuit
items.summary: A central challenge in actuarial science is characterising the distribution of losses generated by an insurance portfolio. Copulas provide a natural framework for modelling joint distributions, but flexible high-dimensional copula fitting and sampling remains challenging in practice.

items.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition
items.summary: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers.

items.title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
items.summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench.

items.title: Syndrome-based Calibration Using Gate-Error Amplification
items.summary: We present Gate-Error Amplification for Recalibration with Syndromes (GEARS), a runtime calibration framework that uses gate-error amplification to efficiently tune control parameters during quantum error correction. Maintaining reliable control of large qubit arrays throughout hours-long computations requires repeated calibration to compensate for hardware drift.

items.title: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands
items.summary: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts strong correlation effects within topological flat bands separated from remote dispersive bands. This separation motivates projection onto the central bands, which greatly reduces the computational complexity of many-body calculations, including momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations.

items.title: The computational complexity of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points
items.summary: We study the computational complexity of estimating observables and sampling from stationary states, or fixed points, of bosonic Lindbladian dynamics with bounded-degree polynomial interactions. While the complexity of transient bosonic dynamics has been investigated, understanding the computational power of bosonic fixed points requires addressing subtleties of infinite-dimensional systems, including the existence, uniqueness, and convergence of stationary states.

items.title: Remote Use of Quantum Machines in the Adversarial Scenario
items.summary: Networked quantum technologies allow users to operate quantum machines hosted by remote servers, but classical commands alone cannot ensure that only the intended user can prepare the useful inputs that activate them. We formulate the problem of adversarial remote use of quantum machines in the framework of quantum resource theories.

items.title: Convex splitting by binary quantum hypothesis testing
items.summary: How many independent quantum systems does it take to hide one system that is correlated with a reference? An observer can measure all the systems together with the reference to detect the correlation.

items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.summary: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the…

items.title: Counterfactual attribution of surface-code failures under non-Pauli noise: dependence on trajectory pairing
items.summary: Under Pauli noise in a stabilizer memory, attributing a quantum error-correction failure to the noise that caused it has a canonical answer; under non-Pauli noise the attribution depends on how trajectories are paired with their counterfactuals. We define a failing shot's cause set, the sites whose removal alone removes the failure, and separate it from pairing-independent net effects.

items.title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
items.summary: Computational homogenization requires repeated solutions of representative volume element (RVE) problems to determine the effective response transferred to the macroscale, including the homogenized stress. Here, we develop a basis-encoded, energy-based variational quantum formulation for linear-elastic computational homogenization.

items.title: Curvature-Calibrated Friction and an Exact Gauge Symmetry for Quantum Hamiltonian Descent
items.summary: A design problem constrained by a partial differential equation can be solved coherently on a quantum computer. The objective is block-encoded rather than measured, and Quantum Hamiltonian Descent consumes it directly.

items.title: Generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states in a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model implemented with Josephson junctions
items.summary: We investigate the generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model (JCM) implemented in a Josephson-junction quantum circuit. We consider a specific superconducting flux-qubit implementation and estimate the resulting two-photon coupling constant.

items.title: Quantum Symmetry and Entanglement Horizons: Theory, Photonic Systems, and Quantum Inspired Data Analytics
items.summary: This book examines the role of translational symmetry in shaping and stabilising quantum entanglement across spatial and temporal domains. Building on foundational concepts from the EPR paradox and Bell’s theorem, it introduces a nodal–antinodal framework to explain coherence preservation and entanglement amplification.

items.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
items.summary: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach.

items.title: Broadening the horizons of quantum-mechanical methods through synergistic approaches
items.summary: Accurately simulating photo-induced dynamics of molecular systems and their spectroscopic fingerprints under environmentally relevant conditions remains a major challenge in theoretical chemistry, requiring a balance between efficient sampling of nuclear motion and accurate electronic structure description for reliable computation of observables. Single-reference methods provide affordable on-the-fly dynamics but cannot describe near-degenerate regions involving the ground state, nor capture spectroscopic…

items.title: Quantum algorithms
items.summary: This chapter highlights quantum algorithms as a gate-based computational framework that exploits superposition, entanglement, and phase-coherent interference to realize demonstrable complexity reductions on selected problems. It begins by formally distinguishing quantum algorithms from classical deterministic and randomized computation through reversible unitary evolution, oracle-based problem access, and the measurement constraint that collapses quantum state information, thereby motivating amplitude-engineering…

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning: Theory, Algorithms, and Practical Implementation
items.summary: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. As quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance, there is a growing need for a rigorous and accessible text that explains how quantum principles can be used to design, analyze, and implement machine learning models.

items.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
items.summary: OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). However, task-based EEG paradigms are limited by mismatches between task demands and patients' residual awareness, as well as the limited individual assessment capacity of machine-learning-based detection frameworks.

items.title: Quantum dynamical transitions when the corresponding classical phase space has a separatrix: extension of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells
items.summary: In classical Hamiltonian systems with a slowly time-dependent parameter, adiabaticity breaks down at a separatrix, leading to probabilistic post-adiabatic transitions between different phase-space regions described by the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard (KNH) theorem. Quantum mechanically, dynamical tunneling allows adiabaticity to persist where it breaks down classically, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing non-trivial.

items.title: Resilience of emergent Hamiltonian quantum memories in the presence of noise
items.summary: Emergent Hamiltonians can freeze an entangled state prepared through coherent evolution, since that state is an eigenstate of the Hamiltonian under which it is then stored. We show that the freedom left in this construction allows the storage spectrum to be adapted to a noisy environment without changing the stored state.

items.title: Certified Separation Between Coherent and Adaptive Temporal Processing of Quantum-Error-Correction Readout
items.summary: Repeated quantum-error-correction readout is normally converted into a classical time series: each syndrome pulse is measured on arrival and only the resulting classical record is retained. Nonorthogonal readout signals raise the question of whether preserving quantum information between rounds can improve the final recovery decision.

items.title: Tunable source of entangled microwaves by nonlinear scattering of magnons
items.summary: We propose a route to prepare entangled states of microwaves propagating in spatially separated transmission lines using the intrinsic nonlinear dynamics of ferromagnetic spin waves (magnons). We first show that a driven magnon mode can produce entangled magnon pairs at low temperatures by spontaneous parametric down-conversion enabled by three-magnon processes.

items.title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
items.summary: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics.

items.title: Accelerating Diffusion Maps on a Quantum Computer: Spectral Filtering and Galerkin PDE Solvers
items.summary: Diffusion maps generalize principal component analysis (PCA) to nonlinear manifolds, enabling spectral dimensionality reduction, geometric data analysis, and elliptic PDE approximation on point clouds. For large datasets of size $N$, however, classical matrix operations incur prohibitive $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ scaling, even when extracting low-dimensional spectral features or targeted scalar observables.

items.title: Qualiaphobic artificial neural networks (and why to build them)
items.summary: This paper introduces qualiaphobic AI: artificial neural network architectures that are hostile to theories of consciousness. I show that qualiaphobia can be well-justified by knowledge about theories of consciousness, like when such theories are trivial or unfalsifiable or contradicted by overwhelming scientific evidence.

items.title: Nonlinear Vacuum Medium Model 4.0: A Falsifiable Nonlinear Substrate Model for Emergent Quantum and Gravitational Dynamics
items.summary: The Nonlinear Vacuum Medium (NVM) Model 4.0 presents a falsifiable theoretical framework investigating whether quantum phenomena, particle-like excitations, electromagnetic behavior, and gravitational dynamics can emerge from the nonlinear organization of an underlying physical substrate. Rather than assuming that quantum fields and effective spacetime geometry are fundamental, NVM examines their possible emergence through collective dynamics governed by a continuous, nonmechanistic medium.

items.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
items.summary: Slow-wave sleep preserves the capacity for spontaneous or stimulus-evoked awakening despite reduced responsiveness, yet how thalamic nuclei coordinate to preserve arousability remains unclear. We analysed six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol anesthesia and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS).

items.title: Generative AI as epistemic technology and post-editing as a form of repair

items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity.

items.title: Structured coherence: A modern perspective on optical coherence as a resource
items.summary: Optical coherence is a well-established branch of physical optics in which the statistical properties of fluctuating optical fields are described in terms of correlation functions over continuous spatial and temporal degrees of freedom (DoFs). Nevertheless, in any practical setting, only discrete DoFs are ever accessible.

items.title: Operationally induced preferred basis in unitary quantum mechanics
items.summary: The preferred-basis problem remains under unitary system–apparatus dynamics, whereas measurements have mutually exclusive outcomes. The present framework places basis selection in the complete preparation–measurement arrangement.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.summary: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field.

items.title: Chronic hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a brain–CSF interface framework for mechanisms, conceptual states, and surgical management
items.summary: Chronic hydrocephalus following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) may be more usefully conceptualized as the cumulative failure of several interacting brain–CSF boundaries than as a single obstructed conduit. A purely mechanical model cannot account for inflammatory CSF secretion, delayed absorptive failure, impaired clearance, altered tissue compliance, or the heterogeneous need for permanent shunting, so we use a brain–CSF interface and compartment framework to organize these observations.

items.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
items.summary: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations.

items.summary: We explore the symmetry properties of Stinespring dilations of single-qubit Pauli channels, addressing both the generic case and the specific examples of phase damping and depolarizing channels. For each scenario, we derive the representation of the Pauli group acting on the Hilbert space of the environment.

items.title: A quantum-classical surrogate model for the collision operator of the lattice Boltzmann method
items.summary: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers.

items.title: Observing Bell inequality violation beyond the qubit bound in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: Correlations allowed by quantum mechanics can defy any classical explanation, with Bell nonlocality standing as their most profound and operationally powerful manifestation. While nonlocality has been demonstrated across a wide range of platforms, in many-body systems it has remained limited to ensembles of qubits, leaving the observation of higher-dimensional multipartite Bell correlations an open challenge.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Negative quasiprobability trajectories for Bell-diagonal states under local decoherence
items.summary: The fluctuation theorem (FT) relates microscopic trajectory distributions to macroscopic averages. Using quasiprobability trajectories, this framework has recently been extended to quantum information dynamics.

items.title: Spiking the mind: Rethinking the role of cortical feedback in visual mental imagery.
items.summary: Recent research has revealed similarities between visual mental imagery and visual perception. Visual imagery is supported by cortical feedback involving multiple visual areas, including the primary visual cortex, and functionally interacts with perception.

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.

items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.
